items.summary: A landmark study projects 24.7 million annual dementia diagnoses by 2050, with women disproportionately affected. Researchers from the University of NSW analyzed data from 18 countries, noting cases will double from 2023 levels. Professor Henry Brodaty emphasized prioritizing women's brain health and addressing risk factors like education gaps and menopause. Matthew Pase called the figures alarming, urging scalable solutions for low-income regions.
items.title: New Study Projects Dementia Surge by 2050

items.summary: An article alleges that the European Union is continuing to facilitate Russian and Iranian energy imports despite sanctions. A senior EU source claims that a legal exemption for crude oil from the Caspian Pipeline Consortium allows Russian and Iranian oil to be blended and laundered as Kazakh oil. The source states that Kazakhstan's domestic production cannot account for the surge in CPC volumes, suggesting illicit flows. Furthermore, the article claims Moscow and Tehran plan to pivot to the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline in 2027 to bypass restrictions, a move the source describes as a relief valve for the illicit swap.
items.title: EU Sanctions Loophole Alleged in Russian-Iranian Energy Pipeline Scheme

items.summary: A new study published in Nature Medicine suggests menopause-related biological changes are sudden and 'cliff-like' rather than gradual. Researchers analyzed data from over 300 million laboratory tests involving more than 1 million women in the United States and Israel between 1999 and 2024. However, Australian experts, including Martha Hickey and Elina Safro, urge caution, describing the claim as unnecessarily alarming and noting the study's limitations. While the study indicates accelerated changes began about 15 years prior to menopause, experts emphasize that more research is needed and recommend regular health checks starting in one's 40s.
items.title: Australian Experts Question 'Cliff-Like' Menopause Study Findings

items.summary: Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, unveiled a new defence strategy at the Warsaw Security Forum aimed at making any attack on an alliance member 'utterly futile'. Known as the 'Theory of War', the plan relies on three principles: block, blunt, and break. Endorsed by all 32 NATO members, it combines conventional military capabilities with advanced technologies like drones and artificial intelligence, drawing lessons from conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. Grynkewich emphasized that the strategy is defensive, intended to protect allied territory rather than pursue territorial ambitions, while reaffirming the alliance's 'ironclad commitment to Article 5'.
items.title: NATO Commander Unveils Strategy to Deter Future Attacks

items.summary: Four terrorists, including Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Faizan, were killed in a mine blast while allegedly attempting to infiltrate across the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir's Krishna Ghati sector. The incident occurred near Nangi Tekri, where mines laid as part of the anti-infiltration grid exploded, killing all four on the spot. The other three terrorists were identified as Wakas, Ishtiaq and Asim.
items.title: Four Terrorists Killed in Mine Blast Along Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir

items.summary: The Delhi Police have de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue following recommendations from a Ministry of Home Affairs committee. Historically known as 'Mini India,' the site has hosted diverse protests for decades, including major movements in 2011 and 2023. While the police have designated three new venues—Ramlila ground, Burari ground, and CBD ground—in East Delhi, critics argue these locations are farther from the center of power and lack the symbolic significance of Jantar Mantar. Residents also welcome the move, citing noise and sanitation issues caused by continuous demonstrations. The decision has sparked debate over the balance between the right to dissent and the need for peaceful urban environments.
items.title: Delhi Police De-notify Jantar Mantar as Protest Site Amid Calls for Alternatives

items.summary: Jason Horowitz, an American reporter who grew up in Queens, moved to Rome believing Italy's best days were behind it. However, after covering neofascism, financial crises, and immigration for 25 years, including as The New York Times' Rome bureau chief, he found Italy's issues were a harbinger for the rest of the industrial world. Kirkus Reviews describes his memoir as charming and instructive, offering a mix of forewarning and reassurance.
items.title: Jason Horowitz Reflects on His Decades of Reporting in Rome

items.summary: Pakistani authorities detained hundreds of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) members in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Monday, October 12, 2026, following the imposition of emergency rule on Sunday. Police officials stated that 278 PTI members were detained since the emergency declaration, which the government attributed to deteriorating security and militant attacks. The PTI-led provincial government was disbanded, and Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was placed in protective custody. While the government claims the measures are necessary for security, PTI leaders and supporters describe them as undemocratic and a power grab. Protests in support of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan have faltered, with crowds on Monday significantly smaller than previous demonstrations. A driver, Saeed Khan, noted that the rule has caused difficulties for children, businesses, and internet connectivity.
items.title: Pakistan Detains Hundreds of PTI Members as Emergency Rule Takes Hold

items.summary: A new FamilyMart commercial starring Lady Gaga has revived a Japanese advertising tradition of using Hollywood celebrities to promote products. The ad, which shows Gaga performing various tasks like mopping and restocking shelves, aims to increase job applications for the convenience-store chain. FamilyMart currently faces a labor shortage, with about 30% of its 16,455 outlets lacking sufficient personnel. The campaign highlights a broader economic issue in Japan, where finding labor remains a challenge. Lady Gaga's participation joins a long list of Hollywood stars who have appeared in Japanese commercials to promote various brands.
items.title: Lady Gaga Revives Japanese Commercial Tradition Amid Labor Shortage

items.summary: Silicon Valley executives expressed enthusiasm for President Trump's deregulatory approach to artificial intelligence during Tech Week in San Francisco. The administration signed a voluntary safety pact with major tech firms, though critics argue it lacks the enforcement of previous mandates. While defense spending on AI is projected to reach $13.5 billion, researchers and former officials warn that self-regulation has failed to ensure safety. The FTC has opened investigations into leading companies, and Congress continues to push for stricter oversight as the industry expands.
items.title: Tech Leaders Celebrate Trump's Hands-Off AI Policy Amid Safety Concerns

items.summary: The European Commission has selected 46 new strategic projects for critical raw materials across 16 member states, including three focused on lithium extraction. These projects, alongside previously approved initiatives, aim to bolster the EU's supply chain and reduce dependence on single suppliers. The selection includes proposals for extraction, processing, and recycling of various materials such as nickel, cobalt, and rare earth elements. The European Commission stated that these projects are intended to strengthen European value chains and meet specific benchmarks for extraction and processing set by the Critical Raw Materials Act.
items.title: European Commission Selects 46 New Strategic Projects for Critical Raw Materials

items.summary: Nepali rescuers searched for five people missing after fresh flash floods hit central Nepal. These floods swept away over 200 houses and five bridges along the Budhi Gandaki River. The area is still recovering from devastating floods triggered by a mountain glacial collapse on August 26, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 5,000 missing.
items.title: Flash floods in central Nepal leave five people missing amid ongoing recovery efforts

items.summary: Diplomats from 196 parties are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity summit to finalize legal texts under the UN Convention on Biological Diversity. The meeting addresses the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, noting that countries are not on track to meet 22 of its 23 targets. Key discussions will focus on a global review and finance, with global south countries pushing for increased funding and a separate financial mechanism.
items.title: Diplomats gather in Armenia for COP17 biodiversity negotiations

items.summary: Hundreds of French supermarkets suffered a cyber attack causing refrigeration units to overheat and spoil food. Intermarché and Coopérative U confirmed hundreds of stores were affected, with temperatures reaching 50C. Authorities launched an investigation into the large-scale incident targeting essential food supply equipment.
items.title: Cyber Attack Disrupts French Supermarket Refrigeration Systems

items.summary: On Maxxen Day 2026, Maxxen Energy opened its factory in Türkiye, showcasing what it calls the most advanced BESS facility in Europe. The company reported delivering over 600 MWh across 20+ projects in nine months, capturing nearly 5% of the European grid-scale BESS market. Ruben Valiente, Managing Director, highlighted the event's success and the company's rapid growth, noting its membership in SolarPower Europe.
items.title: Maxxen Energy Opens Advanced BESS Factory in Türkiye

items.summary: Robert Hall and Michael Woodford received the 2026 Nobel economics prize for developing models that help central bankers stabilise economies. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded them $1.2m (£900,000) for creating New Keynesian frameworks that improve policy tools. Their work, used globally since 2008, aids in managing shocks like energy crises.
items.title: Hall and Woodford Win 2026 Nobel Economics Prize for Stabilisation Models
